taxYearRuns: 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027 — VED rates change on 1 April (Finance Act uprating); the historic-vehicle tax exemption date also rolls forward each 1 April. MOT fees and rules are not tied to the tax year.
jurisdiction: United Kingdom for vehicle tax (VED, administered by DVLA). MOT figures are Great Britain (England, Scotland, Wales): Northern Ireland runs its own MOT scheme (DVA) with different rules, fees and processes.
refreshRule: Calendar-driven (cadenceDays: null). VED rates and the historic-vehicle build-date cutoff change on 1 April each year (Finance Act, announced at the preceding Autumn Budget — the HMRC tax information and impact notes appear on gov.uk on Budget day, the rate-tables page is rewritten shortly before 1 April). MOT maximum fees have been unchanged since 2010; the MOT guide is re-checked when the weekly watcher reports a change. nextScheduledRefresh is set by hand to the next 1 April; a Budget announcement in between is a reason to add the following year's file early.
verificationMethod: Every figure was read on verifiedDate from the gov.uk page named in its `source` (the guide pages and the HMRC policy paper were fetched with curl, User-Agent databutler-curation/1.0, both as HTML and through the gov.uk content API https://www.gov.uk/api/content/<path>; all returned HTTP 200 on 2026-10-04; content-API `updated_at` 2026-09-09 for vehicle-tax-rate-tables, getting-an-mot and historic-vehicles). `quote` reproduces the table row or sentence the value was taken from, columns separated by " | ". `previous` (2025-26) values were read from the UK Government Web Archive (National Archives) captures of the same gov.uk pages named in previous.source, taken 30 May – 4 June 2025, i.e. while the 2025-26 rates were in force; they were not written from memory. Where the live page or the archive capture carries no comparable earlier figure, `previous` is omitted.
licence: gov.uk footer on every page cited: "All content is available under the Open Government Licence v3.0, except where otherwise stated" (https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/doc/open-government-licence/version/3/). National Archives web-archive captures of gov.uk pages are reproduced under the same licence.

ved-expensive-car.title: VED expensive car supplement (list price over £40,000; over £50,000 for zero-emission cars from 1 April 2026)
ved-expensive-car.notes: An additional annual amount on top of the standard rate, charged for five years from the second time the vehicle is taxed, for cars and motorhomes registered on or after 1 April 2017 whose list price (published price before first registration, before discounts) exceeds the threshold. From 1 April 2026 the threshold for zero-emission cars is £50,000 (HMRC policy paper, Budget 2025); it stays £40,000 for all other cars. Zero-emission vehicles registered before 1 April 2025 do not pay it at all.

ved-electric.title: VED for electric (zero-emission) cars — taxable since 1 April 2025
ved-electric.notes: Electric cars, vans, motorcycles and tricycles have paid vehicle tax since 1 April 2025. A zero-emission car registered on or after 1 April 2017 pays the 0g/km first-year rate when first registered, then the standard rate; the expensive car supplement applies to zero-emission cars registered on or after 1 April 2025 whose list price exceeds £50,000 (threshold raised from £40,000 on 1 April 2026). Zero-emission cars registered 1 March 2001 – 31 March 2017 pay band A (ved-2001-2017). Hybrids are "alternative fuel", not zero-emission, and have always paid.

historic.title: Historic (classic) vehicles — 40-year rolling MOT exemption and vehicle tax exemption date
historic.notes: The vehicle-tax cutoff rolls forward one year each 1 April: for 2026-27 a vehicle built before 1 January 1986 (or, build date unknown, first registered before 8 January 1986) can be put in the historic tax class; the keeper must apply (Post Office, V5C) and must still tax the vehicle each year at £0. MOT exemption needs no application but is lost if "substantial changes" have been made. Not exempt from tax if used for hire or reward or commercially.

figures.label: Vehicle tax exemption: built before
figures.quote: You can apply to stop paying for vehicle tax from 1 April 2026 if your vehicle was built before 1 January 1986. You must tax your vehicle even if you do not have to pay.

previous.quote: If your vehicle was built before 1 January 1985, you can stop paying vehicle tax from 1 April 2025.

figures.label: Vehicle tax exemption when the build date is unknown: first registered before
figures.quote: If you do not know when your vehicle was built, but it was first registered before 8 January 1986, you can still apply to stop paying vehicle tax.

previous.quote: If you do not know when your vehicle was built, but it was registered before 8 January 1985, you do not need to pay vehicle tax from 1 April 2025.

mot.title: MOT: when it is due, maximum fees, early renewal, retests and exemptions (Great Britain)
mot.notes: Maximum fees are set in regulations and have not changed since 2010 (the 2025 archive capture shows the same figures); there is no VAT on the fee. A car's first MOT is due on the third anniversary of registration, then annually. The page says an MOT can be taken up to a month minus a day early and keep the same renewal date — not ten months. Northern Ireland has different rules (not covered).
